pages.text: Two plates a hair apart exclude vacuum modes from the gap: a Casimir pressure P = π²ħc/(240a⁴) pushes them together, and the vacuum between them holds negative energy. At about 30 µm that energy density equals the dark energy of the universe.
$(thing)Set$(): Plate gap a, Plate area, Cycle rate, Plate stiffness.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Plate parallelism error: the effective gap is a·(1 + 0.5%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Casimir pull-in: the plates snap together; Thermal photons swamp the vacuum signal: cool the plates; The plate stack is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Plate area swept per second.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective gap: a_eff$(br)Casimir pressure: P = π²ħc/(240a⁴)$(br)Vacuum energy density: |u| = π²ħc/(720a⁴)$(br)Energy density / ρ_Λ: log₁₀(|u|/ρ_Λ)$(br)Force gradient: dF/da = 4PA/a$(br)Thermal wavelength: λ_T = ħc/kT$(br)Extracted power: P = |u|·A·a·f
